races.name: Sky Bet Strensall Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Damysus
runners_data.note: Won twice at 9f on Good ground including a Listed success, genuine hold-up profile under James Doyle and trained by Gosden — 28 days fresh is fine, and the step to soft-ish ground suits a horse who stays strongly; the one to beat for closers.
runners_data.comment: Damysus shaped with plenty of encouragement on his last run when third, and his back-to-back wins in recent starts underline his class; he has run over today's trip and, rated 122, he looks the one to beat from stall five.

runners_data.name: Archivist
runners_data.note: Recent 8f winner under Callum Rodriguez, races prominently but has a patchy record in similar going (0W3P); trainer hit rate at 14 days is modest and with a big field he may find himself squeezed for room at a crucial stage.
runners_data.comment: Archivist has won twice in his last five starts, including last time out, and has run over today's trip, but his inconsistent record and a rating of 107 ranked ninth of thirteen make him hard to recommend with confidence here.

runners_data.name: Dividend
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose form has tailed off from a peak earlier in the season, finishing 6th and 7th in his last two; Rossa Ryan takes over and the 9-10f good-ground profile is fine but he needs to reverse a slide in form.
runners_data.comment: Dividend has finished seventh and sixth in his last two starts, and though he was third three starts back, our figures rank him tenth of thirteen in this field, making him very hard to fancy despite the experience over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Expanded
runners_data.note: Long 97-day absence for the O'Brien yard is the key angle; Ryan Moore takes the ride and the horse handles soft well with a 2nd on soft in the recent past — hold-up profile makes him a player if the gap appears, but the layoff introduces doubt.
runners_data.comment: Expanded has shown consistent placed form, finishing second in each of his last two starts, though he is yet to win in recent starts and returns after a 97-day absence; he has run over today's trip before and carries 133 lb from stall one.

runners_data.name: Jonquil
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a 1st from 8f on good ground but inconclusive recent form in bigger fields; Colin Keane is a quality booking but the horse has placed only three times in last five starts at this class level and has no standout soft-ground evidence.
runners_data.comment: Returned to form with a third last time out after struggling to land a blow in his two prior starts, and he has run over today's trip before; the 133 lb burden is a stiff ask, though 22 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Naqeeb
runners_data.note: Six-year-old who won at 10f on soft (Going concern is actually a positive here — 1W1P in similar conditions); Ryan Sexton is a quieter booking for this level but the veteran's ability to handle testing ground and his genuine hold-up style make him interesting.
runners_data.comment: Naqeeb was a convincing winner four starts back and ran well for second two starts back, showing he retains ability; experience over today's trip and going bolsters his claims, though a 42-day absence and stall 13 under 133 lb are the factors to weigh.

runners_data.name: Persica
runners_data.note: Won at 10f on Good and placed twice more at that trip; Richard Hannon runner races prominently and his soft-ground form shows a 2nd on soft — he gets to the front of the prominent group and if Hankelow weakens he is best placed of the chasing pack.
runners_data.comment: Persica arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip and going, with his 118 rating underscoring a strong threat from stall seven; the main concern is whether 133 lb proves too stiff a burden.

runners_data.name: Point Lynas
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's 7-year-old is a natural prominent racer whose form at this trip is underwhelming (0W0P in similar going), and the congested early field means Jamie Spencer is unlikely to get the position he needs — that role mismatch suppresses his chance materially.
runners_data.comment: Point Lynas was a fine second last time out and has run over today's trip and going, while our rating of 118 marks him out as a leading player from stall four; the worry is he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Ridari
runners_data.note: George Scott runner with solid soft-ground experience (2W4P on soft/heavy), prominent style suits the expected race shape if he can slot in just behind Hankelow; 70-day break is the one question mark, but the form profile on testing ground is genuinely strong.
runners_data.comment: Ridari showed his hand with a win four starts back, and he has run into a place three starts back, leaving him open to more improvement as an unexposed type returning after 70 days off.

runners_data.name: Geryon
runners_data.note: The three-year-old carries a 4lb age allowance and races prominently; Gary Carroll has a horse who has been consistently placed (2nd in three of last five on good ground) — the lighter weight and prominent style make him competitive if the pace is sustainable.
runners_data.comment: Placed second last time out and a winner two starts back, Geryon arrives in decent nick after 23 days and has run over today's trip, though his ranking of eighth in a field of 13 suggests he faces a stiff ask at 129 lb.

runners_data.name: Hankelow
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner who sets the entire tactical shape of this race; K.R. Burke's three-year-old won on good ground and is uncontested for the lead — 83 days off is the concern, but if he finds his rhythm on the soft turf he is the hardest horse to beat on shape alone.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last two starts and ranked well down on our figures, Hankelow is hard to fancy, though he has run over today's trip before and a return from 83 days off could freshen him up.

runners_data.name: King Of Earth
runners_data.note: William Haggas has a natural front-runner who wants to dominate, but this field is too deep in prominent types for Cieren Fallon to claim that position easily — his best form comes when bowling along in front, and being pushed back compromises him significantly; treat the midfield map position as a structural disadvantage, not a natural fit.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well adrift of the field on our figures, King Of Earth faces a stiff ask, though he arrives in good heart after back-to-back wins in his last two starts and has experience of today's trip and conditions.

runners_data.name: Saber Strike
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand rides another Haggas three-year-old who has won twice but from a front-running position that will be very hard to secure here; his true style is pace-setter rather than mid-pack racer, and the redistribution into the pack means he is a horse racing in conditions that actively work against his strongest attribute.
runners_data.comment: Saber Strike arrives on the back of a third two starts back and a pair of wins in his last five, giving him credible recent form, though a sixth three starts back and a fourth last time out are harder to overlook; he has run over today's trip and returns fit enough at 22 days, but a stall-12 draw and 126 lb are factors to weigh.

races.paceDynamic: Hankelow is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate a controlled, unhurried gallop from the front — particularly relevant on Good to Soft ground over 1m1f where a horse allowed to stride into a rhythm from flagfall can be very hard to dislodge. Persica, Archivist, Dividend, Ridari and Geryon all want to race prominently, meaning there will be scrapping for position in the early stages, but Hankelow should be able to slot into a sustainable lead ahead of this group without any single rival able to comfortably press him throughout. The field contains more true prominent types than the race shape can accommodate: Point Lynas, Saber Strike and King Of Earth are genuine front-of-race horses who will be shuffled wider and further back than they would like, compromising their effectiveness. This race shape — a controlled front-runner dictating to a congested midfield on testing ground — strongly favours late-running hold-up horses who can track the tempo and find a clean run through a compressed midfield in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hankelow Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Hankelow gets a clean break, settles into an uncontested rhythm and the pace remains honest but never brutal.
scenarios.body: Hankelow, unchallenged on a Good to Soft surface he handles, sets fractions that suit his stamina profile and uses his positioning advantage to stay out of trouble throughout; hold-up horses must either find room through a bunched midfield or lose too much ground to reel him in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Sweep Through
scenarios.trigger: If the early exchanges produce enough genuine gallop to string the field out and clear gaps appear in the home straight.
scenarios.body: With a legitimate pace set by Hankelow and prominent types getting in each other's way, the closers track into improving positions off the turn and pick off tiring rivals in the final two furlongs on ground that rewards sustained stamina; this scenario is the natural beneficiary of a compressed, traffic-heavy midfield.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely steady enough that a prominent type can travel wide in a good position and kick clear in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A horse like Geryon or Ridari, sitting just off the leader in a comfortable spot, exploits the lack of fierce competition for the lead by producing a well-timed burst when rivals from further back are still navigating traffic; works best if the hold-up horses find themselves stuck behind a wall of horses through the turn.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the battle for prominent positions early becomes sufficiently scrappy that the tempo turns erratic and the race fragments into sections.
scenarios.body: The redistributed prominent types — Saber Strike, King Of Earth and Point Lynas — are racing out of their preferred roles and if they push forward anyway they could create a ragged, uneven gallop that scrambles the race shape unpredictably; horses with versatile tactical profiles and strong trainers benefit most from this confused scenario.

watchPoints.text: Hankelow's front-running position is the keystone of the entire race shape — watch the first furlong to see whether any of the prominent types challenge him for the lead, as any pressure there dramatically changes the complexion of the race.

Saber Strike, King Of Earth and Point Lynas are all natural front-of-race horses who cannot all get their preferred position — watch how aggressively their jockeys push forward early, as a scrappy battle for the first three spots could compromise all three and inject erratic tempo.

Expanded's 97-day layoff for the O'Brien yard with Ryan Moore aboard needs monitoring in the paddock — if the horse looks short of work, the absence is a genuine risk even if the profile otherwise fits this race shape well.

The Good to Soft ground (reported as such across the card) is softer than the declared Soft, which marginally helps genuine stayers and horses with proven soft-ground records — Ridari, Naqeeb and Damysus all tick that box more reliably than several rivals.

Damysus wears headgear (hood, per hg:p) — watch whether this settles the hold-up runner in the early stages, as a calm passage through the compressed midfield is essential for horses racing from off the pace in this scenario.

races.name: Sky Bet Melrose Handicap Stakes (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Limestone
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's lightly raced improver arrives after two wins from three starts on Good ground and a sole soft-ground run that yielded only sixth — his going profile is the key question, but Ryan Moore's booking and a prominent, patient style suit this test of stamina perfectly.
runners_data.comment: Limestone has won four of his last five starts and arrives here as the one to beat, with experience of today's trip and going working in his favour; the 39-day absence is the only minor query, but his class — underlined by a 112 rating — makes him hard to oppose.

runners_data.name: Infraad
runners_data.note: Won at 1m2f on Good and placed on Soft at 1m, so the step up to 1m6f on today's easier going introduces genuine stamina uncertainty; Tom Marquand rides and the Haggas yard is firing, but this trip could stretch him.
runners_data.comment: Infraad arrives on the back of a win last time out, with two victories in his last five starts underlining his consistency, and 24 days between runs suggests he returns fresh; the chief concern is that our rating of 96 leaves him marginally to find on the figures.

runners_data.name: Into The Light
runners_data.note: William Buick and Appleby combine with a horse who won over 1m3f on Good last time; his York form is unknown but he travels prominently, handles fast tracks well, and the softening ground is the main concern for a horse who won on Tapeta at Meydan.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and has placed twice in his last five starts, but an unplaced effort two starts back is the caveat; Into The Light carries 126 lb off an official mark of 96, though a trainer firing at 42% keeps connections firmly in the mix.

runners_data.name: Tierra Del Toro
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett horse who won a Salisbury novice on Standard and placed on Soft — James Doyle takes the ride — but four of his last five runs ended in defeat and his form string suggests he flattens out when the pressure mounts.

runners_data.name: Mythical Bay
runners_data.note: Two wins from his last three and a strong soft-ground record (1W1P) make him one of the best profile fits in the race; Oisin Murphy in the saddle adds horsepower and his stamina at 1m6f was confirmed by a recent 1m6f Goodwood win.
runners_data.comment: Mythical Bay arrives here in sparkling form, winning two on the spin and recording three wins in his last five starts, and he has experience of both today's trip and conditions. The 49-day absence is the one question mark against him.

runners_data.name: Galilean Quality
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's three-year-old has won twice over 1m4f-1m6f on Good and Tapeta, arrives 42 days fresh, and Sam James is an underrated jockey booking; needs to confirm soft-ground effectiveness but his style of racing prominently suits.
runners_data.comment: Galilean Quality has winning form in recent starts, scoring three times in his last five — though a sixth two runs back is a note of caution — and has run over today's trip before; the 42-day absence and a midfield ranking of eighth from seventeen make this a measured each-way proposition rather than a banker.

runners_data.name: My Ballyquinn
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's progressive colt has won twice over 1m6f at Goodwood and Leicester, all on Good — he has no form beyond Good in the going description, making this soft test an unexposed variable, though Mark Winn knows this yard well.
runners_data.comment: Consistent performer who has winning form in his recent starts — a winner two starts back and again four starts back — and he has run over today's trip before, though his last outing was a month ago and 119 lb is no featherweight assignment.

runners_data.name: Glory Road
runners_data.note: Beckett's consistent type with two soft-ground placed efforts to his name; Edward Greatrex takes the mount, and while his instinct is to race prominently, the overcrowding in that group means he is likely to find himself in midfield territory, racing further back than he wants.
runners_data.comment: Glory Road arrives on the back of solid recent form — a winner last time out and placed in each of his other three starts — though a speed rating of 79 and a ranking of seventh of seventeen suggest he faces stiffer opposition here despite his 118 lb burden sitting manageably enough.

runners_data.name: Sharkeyboy
runners_data.note: W.P. Mullins sends this one across in good form but all four runs on record came on Good or Good to Soft — wearing a hood — and Saffie Osborne picks up the ride; a front-of-midfield operator by nature but squeezed out of that slot by the prominent traffic.
runners_data.comment: Sharkeyboy arrives here 26 days fresh, with two runner-up finishes in his last four starts showing he can threaten the podium, yet he remains yet to win in that spell and a pair of fifths temper expectations somewhat, though a trainer firing at 40% is a notable plus.

runners_data.name: Who's Lope
runners_data.note: The one confirmed front-runner in the field; Nicola Currie has ridden him before and he has won over 1m6f on Good, placing twice at the trip — his role is to dictate, and on soft ground at this trip the question is whether he is caught too far from home.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well adrift of his rivals on our figures, Who's Lope faces a stiff ask here, and the 56-day absence adds a fitness query; that said, he does arrive in fair recent nick — second last time out and a winner two starts back — and has run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Baltic Fleet
runners_data.note: Ian Williams runner who has run three times in the last two weeks, finished third most recently, and wears a visor; his recent busy schedule raises fitness-versus-fatigue questions and, while naturally prominent, finds himself shuffled back in this crowded field.
runners_data.comment: Baltic Fleet has been placed in four of his last five starts but pulled up in between, and a trainer operating at just 5% over the past fortnight is a concern; yet to win in recent starts, though he handles today's going and runs off 116 lb.

runners_data.name: Devil's Peak
runners_data.note: John and Thady Gosden pair this blinker-wearing hold-up horse with Tyler Heard; has won over 1m3f on Good and placed at that trip on Stamina track — a genuine hold-up style that fits naturally in the rear and could benefit most if the pace scenario compresses late.
runners_data.comment: Devil's Peak shaped well when second last time out and was a winner two starts back, yet that fifth three starts back hints at inconsistency; he has going experience in his favour and returns on a reasonable 22-day break, though ranked 12th of 17 on our rating he faces a stiff ask here.

runners_data.name: Bay Of Stars
runners_data.note: Dermot Weld sends across a horse who has placed three times on Good/Soft at 1m5f-1m6f, with Ray Dawson aboard; wears a hood and races prominently by instinct, but with so many similar types in the field, he is unlikely to get close enough to the pace to race on his best terms.
runners_data.comment: Bay Of Stars ranks 15th of 17 on our figures, making him hard to fancy, and he has not run for 63 days; however, he was a winner three starts back and arrives here in decent recent nick with a third last time out.

runners_data.name: Steel Raven
runners_data.note: Adrian Keatley's runner shows a win over 1m2f on Good and placed efforts on Soft — the step up in trip and the step up in company against OR 85-105 rivals are both notable asks; naturally prominent but displaced to the middle by overcrowding, limiting his effectiveness.
runners_data.comment: Ranked near the foot of the field on our figures, Steel Raven is hard to fancy despite a win two starts back; his sixth last time out is the more recent message, and while he has run over today's going before, the ratings profile offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Vantage Code
runners_data.note: Emmet Mullins sends a hold-up horse with a soft-ground win over 1m6f at Leopardstown — the most relevant course-type and going form in the field for a genuine backmarker; wears a hood, Rory Cleary rides, and the trip and conditions suit his profile well.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 14 of 17 on our figures, Vantage Code faces a stiff ask, yet his recent form reads more brightly — a winner last time out and placed in two of the four starts before that, with experience over today's trip and ground counting in his favour.

runners_data.name: Eniac
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's Cam Hardie-ridden runner has struggled for wins lately (form: 54933) but consistently fills placing positions; a natural hold-up horse on Good and Soft, his recent placed efforts at 1m4f-1m6f suggest he stays but he may just lack the class to win at OR 82.
runners_data.comment: Consistent enough to have finished third in each of his last two starts, Eniac has run over today's trip and going before, but a trainer in lean form at 1/23 over the past fortnight and a winless recent sequence are the checks against him here.

runners_data.name: Probation
runners_data.note: Kevin Philippart de Foy's progressive front-runner won twice in quick succession, most recently over 1m4f on Good — Harry Vigors takes the five-pound claim — but he is a horse who wants to be near the pace, and this crowded field is likely to see him unable to get close enough to operate on his preferred terms.
runners_data.comment: Ranked last on our figures and up against 16 rivals, Probation faces a stiff ask, though back-to-back wins in his last two starts and a 30-day turnaround suggest he arrives in career-best form and with live fitness, having also run over today's trip before.

races.paceDynamic: Who's Lope is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with just one horse willing to lead, sets a solo, unchallenged gallop over 1m6f on Good To Soft ground at York — a track that rewards horses who travel comfortably through the race rather than those who have to make up ground from the rear. The prominent pack is severely congested: Limestone, Infraad, Into The Light, Tierra Del Toro, Mythical Bay, Galilean Quality, and My Ballyquinn all want to race close to the pace, creating near-certain traffic friction and positional scrapping between the 2f and 3f poles. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — Glory Road, Sharkeyboy, Bay Of Stars, Baltic Fleet, Steel Raven, and Probation are genuine prominent horses forced into midfield, diluting the field's ability to produce a true late-pace scenario. Tactical verdict: a steady-to-honest solo lead with a bunched prominent group creates a race that will be controlled and measured, favouring horses who can travel prominently in the first half of that group without getting buried, quicken once the front-runner is reeled in around two out, and sustain their effort on this stamina-testing ground — the on-pace prominent profile wins this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Group Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack settles cleanly behind Who's Lope and the race develops at an honest but not brutal gallop, allowing those travelling in the first wave to pounce at the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Who's Lope sets an uncontested but genuine enough gallop that the race unfolds in a line, and the horse with the most residual quality in the prominent group — racing on the right terms in their natural style — wins a straightforward sustained-gallop contest.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Late
scenarios.trigger: If Who's Lope sets a dawdling early gallop and the prominent runners fail to accelerate until very late, compressing the race into a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A falsely-run 1m6f over soft ground catches the prominent group flat-footed when the tempo suddenly lifts in the final quarter-mile, allowing the genuine hold-up horses at the back to benefit from a late surge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos, Wide Movers
scenarios.trigger: If the congested prominent group causes significant interference between the 3f and 2f poles, forcing some runners to swing wide to find a clear passage.
scenarios.body: Horses who can be produced wide and away from the scrimmage avoid the trouble, while those buried on the rail or caught in traffic lose several lengths at a crucial stage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Horse Breaks Free
scenarios.trigger: If one of the true prominent horses mapped to midfield — most likely Glory Road or Probation — actively pushes forward early enough to secure a position closer to Who's Lope than their mapped slot suggests.
scenarios.body: Racing closer to the pace than their drawn position implies, such a horse effectively gets into the race on their natural terms, but the extra energy expended forcing the issue on soft ground makes it a hard-won effort at a distance already near their limit.

watchPoints.text: Prominent traffic explosion 2-3 out — with seven horses competing for the same four or five positions behind Who's Lope, expect significant checking, bumping and position-swapping around the turn into the straight that could cost several runners meaningful lengths.

Who's Lope's gallop control is pivotal — if Nicola Currie elects to crawl early in a 17-runner soft-ground handicap, the race could turn into a falsely-run sprint that turns the form book upside down and benefits Devil's Peak and Vantage Code.

Limestone's sole soft-ground run produced a poor effort (6th); Ryan Moore may ride him very prominently to avoid relying on his stamina reserves through the going, but if the surface inconveniences him he could stop quickly in the straight.

Bay Of Stars and Glory Road both want to race prominently but are mapped to midfield — watch for either making an aggressive move forward from the gate, which could escalate the pace or cause further congestion in the first half of the race.

Vantage Code is the only runner with a winning effort at 1m6f specifically on soft ground, and hold-up horses with that combination are historically underestimated in saturated prominent fields — worth monitoring where Rory Cleary positions him in the early stages.

races.name: Sky Bet City Of York Stakes (Group 1)

runners_data.name: Lake Forest
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for William Haggas and Cieren Fallon who has winning form over 7f on good ground but has zero wins or places from two runs on similar going — soft conditions are genuinely concerning, and from a wide field she will need everything to fall perfectly in a race this congested.|
runners_data.comment: Lake Forest won two starts back and has run over today's trip, carrying 134 lb from stall five as the top-rated runner in the field; the worry is that seventh last time out suggests his form can be in and out.

runners_data.name: Marvelman
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner ridden by P J McDonald for Andrew Balding, with a win on soft ground in his record and strong claims to control this race from the front; his ability to set his own fractions is his primary weapon and he should not be taken for granted at the head of affairs.|
runners_data.comment: Ran second two starts back but ninth three starts back tempers enthusiasm, and he has been out of the frame more often than not in recent starts; has run over today's trip and 25 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh, though 134 lb is a stern ask.

runners_data.name: Native Warrior
runners_data.note: K R Burke's five-year-old carries three wins from five runs on soft-equivalent ground and is a genuine prominent racer by nature, but with six other horses ahead of him for those early spots he is very likely to find himself racing in a position he does not want — his chance is real if he can get cover just behind the leaders, but the redistribution is a material risk.|
runners_data.comment: Native Warrior won last time out and has experience of today's distance and going, but ranked 11 of 14 on our figures and carrying 134 lb after 72 days off, he faces a stiff task here.

runners_data.name: Notable Speech
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's five-year-old with William Buick aboard is rated 124 and the class act in the field, but all five of his recent runs have come on firm or good-to-firm ground — this soft surface is an untested variable, and he has not won on anything close to today's conditions.|
runners_data.comment: Three wins in his last five starts, including a victory two starts back, make Notable Speech a genuine threat here, and he has run over today's trip before; the main risk is the 67-day absence.

runners_data.name: Paborus
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's progressive five-year-old has won three of his last five, including on Tapeta, and wants to race prominently — with the prominent seats oversubscribed he faces a very real risk of having to settle further back than his running style demands, which would blunt his chance considerably.|
runners_data.comment: Paborus has won three times in his last four starts, most recently landing the spoils, though a third two starts back breaks the sequence; he has run over today's trip before, but 56 days off the track and a burden of 134 lb from stall 13 are factors to weigh.

runners_data.name: Powerful Glory
runners_data.note: Richard and Peter Fahey's four-year-old has winning form on soft going and over 6f, but is stepping up to 7f here; Jamie Spencer gives him tactical intelligence in a tricky traffic race and he has a strong recent course win, making him interesting if he secures a clean prominent position.|
runners_data.comment: Powerful Glory won two starts back but that seventh last time out — after a 91-day absence — leaves fitness questions hanging; he has run over today's trip and carries 134 lb from stall nine, a weight that may test his chances of recapturing that winning form.

runners_data.name: Rogue Diplomat
runners_data.note: Harry Davies rides this hold-up horse for James Owen, who carries three wins and two places from five runs on soft-equivalent going — comfortably the best soft-ground profile among the closers — and his two recent placed runs on soft give him genuine credentials if traffic allows him a clean passage.|
runners_data.comment: Rogue Diplomat shaped well enough last time, finishing second, but our rating of 106 leaves him well below the field ranked 12 of 14, and a seventh three starts back does little to inspire confidence; carrying 134 lb from stall 12, the case for him is thin despite experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Satono Reve
runners_data.note: The seven-year-old Japanese raider trained by Noriyuki Hori with Joao Moreira aboard has been racing exclusively over 6f on good ground recently with no wins from 14 attempts on similar going — stepping up to 7f on soft is an entirely new profile, and his claims depend heavily on conditions and trip suiting better than his data suggests.|
runners_data.comment: Satono Reve has been in fine form of late, finishing second twice and third last time out, with a win four starts back adding further substance to his profile; he has run over today's trip before and 124 on our rating marks him a leading danger, though 42 days off the track is the one question to answer.

runners_data.name: Ten Bob Tony
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's five-year-old has won on soft ground over 7f at OR=121, making him highly competitive on both counts today; Kieran Shoemark takes over and if he can slot into a prominent position without burning energy fighting for it, he profiles as one of the most condition-appropriate runners in the race.|
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins give Ten Bob Tony strong recent credentials, and he arrives here fit on 24 days' rest having run over today's trip and going before. Carrying 134 lb from stall 8, a fourth last time out tempers enthusiasm slightly, but his profile makes him a confident selection.

runners_data.name: Flora Of Bermuda
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's five-year-old mare is in fine form with three wins from her last four, but she is by nature a prominent runner who is almost certainly going to find too many horses ahead of her for those spots — Oisin Murphy's horsemanship will be tested in getting her into a workable position from which her form can be expressed.|
runners_data.comment: Flora Of Bermuda arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and has run over today's trip and going, though that unplaced effort three starts back tempers enthusiasm slightly, and 131 lb from stall 10 is no small ask against a competitive 14-runner field.

runners_data.name: Lifeplan
runners_data.note: Declan Carroll's lightly raced three-year-old has won two of three career starts over 6f, all on good ground, and wants a prominent berth that this crowded pace map will struggle to offer her; the step to 7f on soft and Group 1 class make this a very significant ask, with Zak Wheatley requiring everything to fall in her favour.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked near the foot of the field on our figures and carrying a hefty 129 lb from stall 14, Lifeplan is hard to fancy despite a tidy recent sequence that includes back-to-back wins in his last three starts, with a third last time out.

runners_data.name: Power Blue
runners_data.note: Robson De Aguiar's three-year-old won last time over 7f on good ground and is a natural prominent type who finds that slot unavailable in this field — David Egan will need to make a decision early about whether to fight for position or accept a midfield role that does not suit, and neither option is comfortable at this level.|
runners_data.comment: Power Blue won last time out and has run over today's trip, but his recent form also shows a pair of fourths in the two starts before that victory, and 34 days off adds a fitness query; carrying 129 lb from stall seven is the added test here.

runners_data.name: Puerto Rico
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore and Aidan O'Brien's three-year-old has won at Group 1 level and carries strong maiden/conditions form, but his last three runs show a drop-off at the top level with a 0 as his most recent figure; soft ground is untested for him and Moore will need to find a prominent position in a very crowded early order.|
runners_data.comment: Puerto Rico has back-to-back wins in his recent form but has since slipped to unplaced on his latest start, and our rating ranks him last of the 14 runners here, making him hard to fancy despite the experience over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Zavateri
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's three-year-old has won twice over 7f on good ground and Charles Bishop gives him each-way claims at big-race prices; he is a natural prominent type, his soft-ground profile is limited to one run, and he would need the pace to be genuinely searching to bring his staying power into play at the death.|
runners_data.comment: Zavateri won two of his last five starts and catches the eye with a second two runs back, though a fifth last time out and a weight of 129 lb are factors to weigh; he has run over today's trip and going, and draws stall two.

races.paceDynamic: Marvelman is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 14-runner Group 1 field and, with no genuine pressing rival likely to sit on his girth from the jump, he can control tempo from the front on Good to Soft ground at a pace he dictates rather than one forced upon him. Behind him, Notable Speech, Ten Bob Tony, Powerful Glory, Satono Reve, Puerto Rico and Zavateri all want to race prominently, creating a dense, combustible pack of six to seven horses chasing those first two or three spots from the gates, with serious traffic dangers emerging between the two- and three-furlong poles as the field compresses around the turning false straight. Hold-up horses Lake Forest and Rogue Diplomat will be threading through that midfield scrum in the final quarter-mile, requiring clean runs they may not get. This field carries significantly more front-running and prominent energy than the race shape can accommodate — Paborus, Lifeplan, Flora Of Bermuda, Power Blue and Native Warrior are all natural prominent racers who are almost certain to find themselves bumped back into midfield against their will, with Marvelman and Notable Speech best positioned to actually secure the early slots. The tactical verdict is clear: the congested prominent group creates a falsely compressed race that will suit horses racing just off a controlled lead — genuine prominent types who secure a clean position inside the top three or four will be ideally placed, while hold-up horses face a lottery of traffic.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Marvelman Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Marvelman dictates a steady-to-moderate tempo on the soft ground and the prominent pack settles without a pace duel erupting.
scenarios.body: Marvelman sets fractions he is comfortable with, the prominent cluster of Notable Speech, Ten Bob Tony and Satono Reve track him without burning unnecessary petrol, and the race develops into a tactical contest where class and position rule from two out; horses who secured a clean prominent berth get first run and the hold-up horses find traffic when they need space.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Duel, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the congestion behind Marvelman causes one or more prominent types to push forward and force a genuine pace battle through the first three furlongs.
scenarios.body: A contested gallop on soft ground stretches the field significantly by halfway, burning off the prominent runners who had to work to get position, and the race falls apart for those who overcook it; the hold-up horses Lake Forest and Rogue Diplomat, if they get even a slightly clean passage, finish powerfully through a tiring field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Stalemate, Late Burst
scenarios.trigger: If the entire field crawls to the two-furlong mark, creating a sprint-finish bunfight where pace plays almost no role.
scenarios.body: Marvelman's lead evaporates the moment the field quickens simultaneously from three out, and the sprint-finish on soft ground becomes a stamina-and-class test rather than a race shape advantage; a horse with a high cruising speed who can accelerate from the pack wins, favouring the highest-rated animals who kept out of trouble.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Grinds, Stayer Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the going deteriorates further through the card and the pace collapses into a searching test of stamina for a sprint trip.
scenarios.body: Horses with proven soft-ground credentials and strong finishing kicks under stamina pressure move clear as the early pace melts away and the final two furlongs become an attrition examination; Native Warrior and Rogue Diplomat, both with strong soft-ground form, come into sharper focus here.

watchPoints.text: Marvelman and the chasing prominent group — with six-plus horses wanting the same early position, watch for bumping and jostling in the first furlong that could unsettle riders and disrupt Marvelman's rhythm at the front.
Lake Forest and Rogue Diplomat face a high-risk passage through a densely packed midfield from two furlongs out — any pocket they get trapped in at that point effectively ends their race.

Notable Speech's going credentials are entirely untested on soft ground — if the conditions prove beyond him early, William Buick may be on a horse that simply cannot reproduce his best, regardless of how the race unfolds tactically.

Satono Reve lines up with zero wins or places from 14 starts on good-equivalent ground and is now stepping up in trip on soft — monitor how Joao Moreira positions him early, as an aggressive ride would be completely against the evidence.

The congestion of redistributed prominent types — Paborus, Flora Of Bermuda, Lifeplan, Power Blue and Native Warrior — means the first two furlongs on the straight York track could be unusually scrappy for a Group 1; the horse that escapes cleanly into a rhythm by the quarter-mile mark will have a significant tactical advantage over those who burned energy fighting for position.

runners_data.name: Paradias
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse from Alan King who has won on Soft/Standard and placed at 1m6f, so the trip and likely easy ground are not concerns; 50 days off is manageable, and Shoemark is an astute jockey, but form figures of 553 in the last three suggest he is operating at his ceiling.

runners_data.name: Furthur
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Balding and Oisin Murphy — the headgear note (p) is worth tracking — who has placed once in 13 similar-ground runs without winning; the 1m6f trip has proven competitive for him but his soft-ground run last time was only fourth and he is not a natural winner in this company.

runners_data.name: Spinning Wheel
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for the Crisfords who has two wins on Soft and goes well fresh (16 days); will lead or dispute from the outset and is the key pace-setter — soft-ground form figures of 2W3P in four runs are the best credentials of any front-runner here.
runners_data.comment: Spinning Wheel won last time out and has form over today's trip and conditions, with a trainer firing at 32% in the last fortnight working in his favour; the 134 lb burden and an unplaced run two starts back temper enthusiasm slightly.

runners_data.name: Tarriance
runners_data.note: Balding hold-up type ridden by Colin Keane who has placed at 1m5f but not won on soft going; form of 3854 is patchy and 21 days since last run is fine, but this is a step up in class and he has struggled when the race has not set up for him.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Tarriance arrives on the back of a fourth last time out and a third four starts back offers a flicker of encouragement, though carrying 133 lb looks a stiff ask off a rating of 105, and he has experience over today's trip to draw on.

runners_data.name: Mr Hollywood

runners_data.name: Daiquiri Bay

runners_data.name: Hopewell Rock
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Boughey who won at 1m4f on Good and placed on Soft — his soft-ground form record of 1W3P is encouraging; Callum Rodriguez is a competent northern jockey and this trip looks within range, but he needs the race to be run at a genuine pace.
runners_data.comment: Hopewell Rock won last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, but his record in recent starts has been mixed, with a sixth and a ninth in the mix, and 133 lb is no gimme at a rating of 101.

runners_data.name: Emit
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore rides this Joseph O'Brien four-year-old who has placed on Heavy (hg: t) and finished in the frame on eight similar-ground occasions without winning; consistent form figures of 44543 suggest he will be competitive but the lack of a win at this level is a recurring concern.

runners_data.name: Paddy The Squire
runners_data.note: Prominent type for Jardine and Mullen who has placed three times in 15 similar-ground starts and won at 1m2f on Good; the headgear note (tp) is worth noting and he handles this ground, but six-year-old form of 632 in recent starts suggests he is slightly below the best in here.
runners_data.comment: Placed in two of his last three starts, including a second last time out, Paddy The Squire brings distance and going experience to the table, though 49 days off the track and a mark of 104 under 132 lb make this a stiff ask at a deep ranking of 11th.

runners_data.name: Poetic Sound
runners_data.note: Prominent-racer for Lyons ridden by Carroll who has won three times in 11 similar-ground runs — the strongest similar-ground win record of any prominent type in the field outside the front-runners; 57 days off is the only mild query, but a BBA mark of 102 still looks workable.

runners_data.name: Align The Stars
runners_data.note: Johnston-trained prominent racer who has won at 1m6f on Standard and placed at 1m4f on Good; headgear note (p) and a mark of 101 suit a competitive handicap, and 21 days is a routine gap, but his three similar-ground runs show no wins or places.
runners_data.comment: Align The Stars has winning form in recent starts but has finished seventh last time out and ranks well down our figures among a field of 24, making him hard to fancy despite having run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Burdett Road
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by style, placed at 1m2f on Good, whose best form has come with cut in the ground; the field is so deeply held-up that he is likely to race in midfield rather than his natural position at the rear, reducing his ability to produce his characteristic late surge — three places in 15 similar-ground runs without a win underlines a frustrating profile.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Burdett Road brings distance and going experience to the table and returns on a sharp 21-day turnaround, yet his recent finishes make grim reading and a rating of 107 ranks him eighth of twenty-four, leaving him with plenty to prove under 129 lb.

runners_data.name: Beylerbeyi
runners_data.note: Ian Williams hold-up specialist who carries headgear (ht) and has two wins in 15 similar-ground appearances; at six years old with a mark of 101, he is well-credentialled for the trip, but in a 24-runner field his true style is likely to be compromised by the sheer volume of horses who want to come from behind.

runners_data.name: Stressfree
runners_data.note: O'Meara hold-up type who placed at 1m2f on Good but whose recent form of 2708 is inconsistent; one of three Ian Williams-adjacent hold-up horses crowded into the back end of this field, and the redistribution to midfield reflects that the rear of the race cannot accommodate all the closers, which undermines his biggest strength.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Stressfree has struggled for consistency of late — eighth last time out and seventh three starts back — though a second four starts back hints at better, and he arrives with distance and going experience to call on under 127 lb.

runners_data.name: Love Me Tender

runners_data.name: Enemy

runners_data.comment: Ranked near the foot of the field on our figures and representing a trainer in poor form at just 5% over the past fortnight, Dancing In Paris is hard to fancy despite his win last time out; he has run over today's trip and going before, but that is scant consolation given the overall profile.

races.paceDynamic: Spinning Wheel and Square Necker are the two confirmed front-runners in this 24-runner field, and with both holding genuine pace credentials over this trip, they will contest the early lead and ensure an honest, pressure-filled gallop on Good to Soft ground across 1m6f at York. Spinning Wheel has won at 12f on soft and goes well fresh; Square Necker arrives on a hat-trick and will not be surrendering the lead cheaply, so the early exchanges are likely to be genuinely competitive rather than a dawdle. Behind them, Daiquiri Bay, Opportunity, Paddy The Squire, Poetic Sound, Align The Stars, and Klassleader all want to race prominently, meaning the front half of the field will be congested and the pace will be maintained throughout — a thorough test of stamina on the easy ground. The field carries more hold-up and prominent types than can all settle in their natural positions: Burdett Road, Beylerbeyi, Stressfree, Real Dream, Circus Of Rome, and Enemy are true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear is already over-subscribed, and those are unlikely to get the clean, late run their style demands in a field this large. This race shape — a genuinely contested pace, easy ground, and a premium on stamina — strongly favours horses racing prominently in behind the two leaders, able to travel within the race and pick off the front-runners in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Spinning Wheel and Square Necker set a genuine pace and prominent-tracking horses travel fluently to dominate the straight.
scenarios.body: The contested early gallop on soft ground drains the field, and the horses who have settled just off the pace in positions two to five are best placed to pounce when the front-runners tire in the final two furlongs; the stamina-laden 1m6f trip rewards those who travel efficiently without fighting for position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runners Outstay
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves honest enough to string the field out but the two leaders — particularly Square Necker — find reserves no prominent tracker can match.
scenarios.body: Square Necker's hat-trick form and Spinning Wheel's soft-ground wins suggest both have genuine stamina, and if the pace is metronomic rather than suicidal, one of them can ration their effort and hold on as the field fails to close.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fierce enough and the race truly falls apart in the straight, creating a wide-open sprint for home that a late finisher can exploit.
scenarios.body: Emit, Furthur, and Mr Hollywood all have the class and stamina profile to close ground powerfully on soft ground if the race is truly run at a searching tempo; Ryan Moore's positional awareness on Emit and Oisin Murphy on Furthur give both live each-way claims if conditions create the right cut-back.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Midfield Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Square Necker or Spinning Wheel drops away early leaving a false or steadier early pace that benefits resolute stayers from midfield.
scenarios.body: Paradias and Epic Poet both have stamina pedigree at this trip and have run competitively at 1m6f, and a reduced early pace could see midfield horses preserve enough energy to overhaul a tired lead group with a sustained run.

runners_data.name: Evening Saigon
runners_data.note: James Doyle takes over on this Al Jehani-trained four-year-old who has won over this course and trip in good going and shapes as a prominent racer who should travel kindly just behind the speed; soft ground appears within range given prior STA form.
runners_data.comment: Evening Saigon won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, lending solid claims, though a seventh two starts back hints at inconsistency; drawn four carrying 134 lb, he arrives in good order on a 21-day break.

runners_data.name: Far Above Dream
runners_data.note: Won three of his last five starts all on good ground and all over 6f — the soft-going record is limited to a sixth at Goodwood, which is a concern in conditions that will be more testing; Kieran Shoemark is a competent partner if the horse handles it.
runners_data.comment: Far Above Dream won three of his last five starts, including back-to-back victories three and four starts back, but successive below-par efforts since suggest he may be struggling to recapture that form; he has run over today's trip and returns after 21 days, carrying 133 lb from stall 12.

runners_data.name: Fine Interview
runners_data.note: Exceptional soft-ground record with six wins from eleven starts on that surface, and has won on soft over this trip repeatedly — this is unambiguously his best conditions and 77 days off the track is unlikely to blunt a horse trained by Al Jehani in good form; a prominent runner who can travel close enough to benefit from the pace.

runners_data.comment: Ran to a second five starts back and a winner six starts back, but has been out of the frame in his most recent outing; Pocklington has distance and going experience to call on, though carrying 132 lb from stall 10 is no help returning after 28 days.

runners_data.name: King Of Light
