runners_data.comment: Ranked 16 of 20 on our figures, King Of Light has posted three consecutive finishes of sixth or worse in recent starts, making him very hard to fancy despite a win five starts back and experience over today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Toca Madera
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for David O'Meara returning just three days after his last run, and Daniel Tudhope knows his way around York; the horse's recent form on good ground has tailed off and he faces two rivals equally intent on leading — the early battle could drain him entirely.
runners_data.comment: Finished third last time out, though a quick three-day turnaround and 130 lb to carry are testing angles against him; has run over today's trip and a win six starts back hints at capability, but his recent record has been largely mid-pack.

runners_data.name: Flash Harry
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's four-year-old is a natural prominent racer in character but has been mapped to midfield because there simply is not room for every speed horse in this field — his soft-going form is limited to a sixteenth at Haydock and his chance depends on circumstances working in his favour rather than raw ability.
runners_data.comment: Flash Harry has run over today's trip and the trainer is in fine nick at 26% over the past fortnight, but his recent form reads 9th and unplaced in his last two starts, with that sole win coming five starts back, so he carries 130 lb from stall 17 into a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Pure Legend
runners_data.note: Kevin Stott's mount is at heart a horse that wants to race handy, but with the prominent berths all spoken for by confirmed front-runners, he is unlikely to get his preferred position; has won on soft going over 7f and drops back in trip here, which is slightly against him.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and representing a trainer in the grip of a serious lean spell, Pure Legend is hard to fancy despite his win two starts back; sixth last time out does nothing to shorten the odds against a revival.

runners_data.name: Hammer The Hammer
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's four-year-old is one of three confirmed front-runners yet has finished no better than fifth in five recent starts on good ground — the enthusiasm to lead is not matched by the results and Shane Gray will be fighting for the front position against two rivals from the gun.
runners_data.comment: Rated a clear best-in-field at 108 and carrying an official mark of 96, Hammer The Hammer has distance and going experience to call upon and arrives here on a workable 21-day break, yet he is winless in his last five starts and his trainer's current 4% strike rate is a significant concern.

runners_data.name: Realign
runners_data.note: William Haggas has a strong hand in sprints but Tom Marquand's mount is a confirmed prominent-style horse pushed into the midfield on the map because the race has too many speed types; did win over this course and trip on good going and the form is not without merit, but the race shape does not flatter his chances.
runners_data.comment: Showed he can win when landing a success three starts back, but has been unplaced in both runs since, and 130 lb is a stiff weight to carry; has run over today's trip and going, which at least counts in his favour from stall 2 after a 21-day break.

runners_data.name: Air Force One
runners_data.note: P J McDonald's mount is a hold-up specialist who returns quickly from three days ago, with a visor fitted and a solid record on similar going including wins at 5-6f; the rapid reappearance is worth noting but Geoff Oldroyd clearly has the horse tuned up.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and has run over today's distance and going, but three days between runs is a quick turnaround and 130 lb is a stiff burden; he has placed twice in recent starts, so the each-way claims are real, though the turnaround in time is the concern.

runners_data.name: Desert Falcon
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho sends out one of the three confirmed front-runners after a 77-day break — the soft-going record is actually encouraging with a win and two places — but Ryan Sexton will face immediate company from Toca Madera and Hammer The Hammer and the long layoff makes fitness a question.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 17 of 20 on our figures and with a trainer striking at just 5% recently, Desert Falcon is hard to fancy despite having run over today's trip and going before; two disappointing efforts in his last two starts and 77 days off the track compound the concern.

runners_data.name: Red Spells Danger
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's three-year-old carries a penalty for recent winning form and has a tidy record over 6f on good going; prominent in style and has been running consistently at the level, but soft ground experience is absent and David Allan faces a difficult draw in a packed field.
runners_data.comment: Red Spells Danger won last time out and has run over today's trip, but he carries a hefty 129 lb from stall 19, and with the yard firing at just 5% recently and our figures ranking him eighteenth of twenty, he is hard to fancy at this level.

runners_data.name: Coul Angel
runners_data.note: Saffie Osborne's mount has placed repeatedly over 6f on good going and is a natural prominent racer, though the field's surfeit of pace means she is unlikely to secure her preferred tracking slot; Michael Appleby's mare handles this surface adequately but needs things to go smoothly for her in running.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts despite three runner-up finishes, Coul Angel is drawn in stall 20 carrying 128 lb, and ranked 19 of 20 on our figures — hard to fancy, though he has run over today's trip and returns after a fresh 28-day break.

races.paceDynamic: Toca Madera, Hammer The Hammer and Desert Falcon are all confirmed front-runners in a 20-runner field, guaranteeing a strong early gallop over 6f on Good to Soft ground at York — stamina will be tested from the outset and any horse that races too freely or gets involved in positional battles early will pay a price in the final furlong. With eight of the twenty wanting to race prominently, there will be intense jostling for position between the 2f and 3f marks, creating genuine traffic danger and potential for crowding down the centre of the track. The pace scenario strongly favours hold-up horses with a proven soft-ground record who can travel wide, switch off in midfield, and pick up the pieces as the pace-setters tie each other up. Fine Interview, Sondad and Golden Mind — true hold-up or prominent types with credible soft-going profiles — are best placed to exploit a strongly-run race that sets up for horses arriving late with energy in reserve. Several runners listed in prominent positions are in fact redistributed: Flash Harry, Pure Legend, Realign and Coul Angel are natural prominent racers who are unlikely to secure that position given the traffic ahead of them, with Toca Madera and Desert Falcon most likely to actually lead, and Hammer The Hammer pressing for the early splits.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace explodes, closers win
scenarios.trigger: If Toca Madera, Hammer The Hammer and Desert Falcon fight for the lead and set a punishing tempo that burns out the entire prominent group.
scenarios.body: The strong pace on soft ground will drain the field from the front two furlongs out, leaving late-finishing hold-up horses to mow through exhausted rivals in the final 100 yards; horses with proven soft-going stamina and a relaxed early style will have a decisive energy advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent survivor grinds on
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three pace-setters settles fractionally better than the others and establishes a solo lead while rivals waste energy fighting for second.
scenarios.body: A single front-runner dictating at a strong but controlled clip on soft ground can grind relentlessly to the line before closers fully wind up, especially if the field is bunched and held up in traffic at the two-furlong marker; stamina and a high cruising speed become the premium qualities.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield split, class tells
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion causes traffic issues two out and one horse finds a gap at the right moment from a tracking position.
scenarios.body: The chaotic middle section of the race creates a split between horses that find clean air early and those who are checked or squeezed, rewarding a horse with a reliable jockey who can manoeuvre quickly and a high Racing Post Rating to finish it off.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front runner pinches it
scenarios.trigger: If one of the confirmed front-runners, most likely Toca Madera, steals an uncontested lead as rivals are distracted fighting each other for prominent spots.
scenarios.body: Although three-way pace duels typically end in disaster for all parties, a scenario where one horse jumps fastest and is allowed a soft opening split while the others check each other is plausible; on soft ground at York, an unchallenged leader can set a rhythm that is surprisingly difficult to peg back in a big field with traffic.

watchPoints.text: Three confirmed front-runners — Toca Madera, Hammer The Hammer and Desert Falcon — will fight for the lead from the first stride, and the resulting pace war on soft ground is likely to produce an unusually strong tempo that may leave the entire lead group empty inside the final furlong.

With eight of twenty runners seeking prominent positions, severe crowding is likely between the 2f and 3f marks — horses drawn widest and jockeys with the clearest route to the outside (Moore on King Of Light, Murphy on Dance In The Storm) will have a significant positional advantage avoiding the traffic.

Fine Interview has not run for 77 days and Desert Falcon for the same — if either returns ring-rusty, their scenario-defining role changes significantly; trainer Al Jehani has only a 1/7 strike rate in the last 14 days, adding further caution around Fine Interview's readiness.

Stratusnine and Air Force One both run just three days after their last appearance — quick turnarounds in a 20-runner handicap on soft ground create real fitness and freshness risks, and either horse underperforming would alter the traffic dynamics in the prominent group materially.

The soft going at York over 6f will stretch stamina considerably — horses whose recent form is built entirely on good or good-to-firm ground (Far Above Dream, Red Spells Danger, King Of Light) should be watched carefully from the 2f pole to see if they are genuinely coping with conditions or flattening out.

races.name: Julia Graves Roses Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Adonius
runners_data.note: The form line reads 1-1-1-2 with both defeats on Good and wins on Soft — her going record here is excellent, she has led in all starts, and Rebecca Menzies has her spot-on at 24 days; the chief question is whether Hickory Lad allows her a clean lead.
runners_data.comment: Adonius arrives in career-best form, winning three of his last four starts, and has run over today's trip and going before; the chief concern is whether that second last time out signals the start of a slight dip.

runners_data.name: Dance A Jig
runners_data.note: Rossa Ryan takes the ride for Ralph Beckett (5/33 in 14 days, active stable), and her sole win came on Good with placed efforts on Soft — she travels prominently and should find the pace scenario suits if she can slot in just behind the lead battle cleanly.
runners_data.comment: Dance A Jig won last time out and has experience of today's distance and going, making him a serious threat here off 128 lb; the question is whether that weight from stall 11 blunts his finishing kick.

runners_data.name: Dorigo
runners_data.note: Kevin Stott partners this Kevin Ryan runner who has placed twice at 6f and comes back to 5f for the first time; all runs have been on Good or Standard and he drops in trip which is an uncertainty, though the prominent style means he won't be far off the speed.
runners_data.comment: Dorigo has shown a knack for hitting the frame, second two of his last three starts, but a seventh in between and a trainer firing at just 4% of late are real concerns; he's yet to win in recent starts, and while he has run over today's trip, the stable's cold streak is hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Dubai Champion
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore rides a horse that is a natural prominent racer — Ben Haslam's runner has won over 5f on Soft and has strong course-related form, but his position at the rear of the pace map is artificial due to redistribution; expect him to race much closer to the pace than his mapped position implies, potentially making up for any early crowding.
runners_data.comment: Won two starts back and ran second last time out, so Dubai Champion arrives in fair heart; he has run over today's trip and going before, though carrying 128 lb from stall five and a speed rating of 81 leave him with something to find against the top-rated runners.

runners_data.name: El Floridita
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand partners this Nigel Tinkler runner whose only win was on Good ground over 5f, and the form figure of 5-1-2-5 shows inconsistency; prominent style with a stamina-testing pace could suit if she reproduces her best, but soft ground has not been tested.
runners_data.comment: El Floridita shaped well when second two starts back and was a winner three starts back, giving him a solid recent profile over today's trip; back after 24 days and carrying 128 lb from stall 9, he appeals as the one to side with here.

runners_data.name: Hanney Boy
runners_data.note: Headgear (p) noted, and Evanna McCutcheon's yard has no 14-day runners to reference; his sim-going record of 2/5 prominent runs on soft shows he handles it, and his record of five consecutive placed efforts makes him a natural each-way profile in this scenario rather than a winner.
runners_data.comment: Hanney Boy won last time out and has run over today's trip, but a rating of 94 and a speed figure of 68 suggest he sits in the middle of this field, and carrying 128 lb from stall ten gives him little obvious edge.

runners_data.name: Hickory Lad
runners_data.note: Sam James partners a horse who wants to lead — his win at 6f on Soft and recent placed effort at 5f on Good show adaptability — but the form figure of 8 on his most recent run at 6f on Good is a red flag, and contesting the early lead with Adonius on soft ground carries physical risk.
runners_data.comment: Hickory Lad shaped with plenty of promise when a winner three starts back and a runner-up four starts back, and he returns here on a going and distance combination he has already encountered, fit enough after 23 days. The risk is that eighth last time out raises a query over current form.

runners_data.name: Jaan Ki Tukri
runners_data.note: Kieran Shoemark rides for an in-form Clive Cox yard (7/30 in 14 days), but recent form of 10-9 at 6f on Good suggests step back to 5f is essential; headgear worn, and the confirmed front-running tag means she adds to pace pressure without necessarily being the one to benefit from it.
runners_data.comment: Unplaced last time out after winning two starts back, Jaan Ki Tukri ranks ninth of twelve on our figures and faces a stiff ask at 128 lb from stall six, though a trainer striking at 26% in recent weeks and experience over today's trip offer slim crumbs of encouragement.

runners_data.name: Sale Shark
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride for Hugo Palmer (2/40), and Sale Shark's sole win was on Good over 5f — the soft ground is untested, which is the key unknown; prominent style means he can't coast in midfield, and Murphy's ability to find a tactical position could prove the difference.
runners_data.comment: Sale Shark showed he can win at this level, scoring a winner four starts back, but three consecutive finishes of fifth, fifth, and fourth since suggest he's found improvement hard to sustain; he has run over today's trip and the 24-day break leaves fitness an open question.

runners_data.name: Undercover Affair
runners_data.note: David Evans's filly has a win on Good over 5f and a placed effort on soft — she is a genuine prominent racer placed at the rear of the map solely due to field configuration; Saffie Osborne rides, and while the horse's OR of 81 makes her the least-rated contender here, she handles soft and ran 1-3-2 in recent going-relevant runs.
runners_data.comment: Undercover Affair has finished fifth and eighth in his last two starts, and ranked 11 of 12 on our figures he faces a stiff task here; the one genuine bright spot is a win three starts back, and he has run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Roots In Touche
runners_data.note: M.P. Sheehy rides this Adrian Keatley runner who completed a hat-trick at 5f on Good most recently — soft ground is the major unknown for a horse dropping from Ireland, and the lower weight of 123lbs is a small compensation; front-running style in a race with multiple confirmed leaders suggests she will be in the mix early but faces the biggest stamina query.
runners_data.comment: Ranked last on our figures and drawn in stall 12, Roots In Touche faces a stiff ask, though she does arrive on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Silesia
runners_data.note: Shane Gray rides for Kevin Ryan (yard has one winner from 30 in 14 days), and the 59-day absence is the most notable flag in the field; she has placed twice on Soft over 5f and shown consistency, but the layoff combined with four front-running rivals means she must break brilliantly to feature, making her profile speculative.
runners_data.comment: Silesia has been placed in each of her last four starts but remains winless, and with her trainer in poor form (1/28 over the past fortnight) and our figures ranking her tenth of twelve, it is hard to make a compelling case despite her having experience of today's trip and going.

races.paceDynamic: Adonius, Hickory Lad, and Jaan Ki Tukri are all confirmed front-runners in a 12-runner field over five furlongs on Good to Soft ground at York, meaning the tempo from the gates will be fierce and unrelenting — there is no scenario where this race is run at anything other than a strong gallop. With five runners in total seeking prominent positions, congestion in the early stages is almost certain, and those fighting for the rail or a clear lead between the two and three furlong markers face significant interference risk. The soft ground will compound the attrition, turning this into a genuine stamina test that punishes horses expending energy in early position battles. Dubai Champion and Undercover Affair are both natural prominent racers redistributed to the rear of the pace map — the front-running and prominent roles are already over-subscribed, with Adonius most likely to dictate on the basis of recent consistent front-running form, and Hickory Lad the chief threat to her for the early lead. This race shape — a hot pace, soft ground, twelve runners — strongly favours horses who can travel just off the pace in a pocket and produce a sustained finish in the final furlong, making prominent-but-covered or well-organised midfield runners the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hot Pace Suits Stalkers
scenarios.trigger: If Adonius and Hickory Lad fight for supremacy from the gates and the tempo burns out the front-runners inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The contested lead on soft ground drains the pace setters entering the final 100 yards, and horses travelling prominently just behind the battle — like Dance A Jig or El Floridita — pounce with energy in reserve; the softer ground lengthens the closing stages enough to reward those who have been covered up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dominates Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Adonius clears the position battle quickly and establishes a controlled lead without being seriously harassed by Hickory Lad.
scenarios.body: With sole control of the pace, Adonius can dictate a manageable tempo that suits her proven front-running style on soft ground, and her winning form over this exact trip in similar conditions gives her the profile to hold on; the soft ground is not a barrier given her two wins on it.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Battle Collapses Field
scenarios.trigger: If the three-way speed duel between Adonius, Hickory Lad, and Jaan Ki Tukri produces a suicidal early tempo that leaves them all emptying in the last furlong.
scenarios.body: In this scenario the race turns into a true cavalry charge in the final 150 yards, and horses with natural finishing power like Sale Shark or Dorigo, having tracked the carnage from slightly further back, find the most ground opening up late; soft ground extends the advantage to any horse with a clean run and residual stamina.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely extreme and the entire field fills the track making it hard to come from off the pace, but Dubai Champion or Undercover Affair manage to produce a late run from their rear-mapped positions.
scenarios.body: Both horses are naturally prominent in style and are only positioned at the rear due to redistribution, so this scenario requires them to race genuinely against type and find gaps in a packed 12-runner field; the probability is depressed because they are not natural hold-up types and soft ground does not typically produce dramatic late swoops over five furlongs at York.

watchPoints.text: Adonius and Hickory Lad are on a collision course for the early lead — watch for bumping or interference in the first furlong as both jockeys try to establish position, which could compromise the race for the entire prominent group.

Jaan Ki Tukri's recent form of 10th and 9th over 6f makes her early pace contribution unreliable — if she fails to travel from the gates, the anticipated three-way speed duel may not materialise and the tempo could be softer than expected.

Dubai Champion is mapped to the rear but is a natural prominent runner — Ryan Moore is likely to push forward early, creating unexpected crowding on the inside rail between the 4f and 3f markers where traffic is already projected to be at its worst.

Soft ground at York over 5f historically produces times 3-4 seconds slower than Good, lengthening the finish window and reducing the advantage of pure gate speed — monitor whether horses with stamina pedigrees (Dance A Jig, Hanney Boy) are drifting in the market, as that would confirm punter confidence in the pace scenario.

Roots In Touche carries 5lbs less than the main field and is unproven on soft — if she fails to stride out freely in the first furlong on the testing ground, her front-running chance evaporates quickly and she becomes a non-factor in the pace shape entirely.

races.name: Sky Bet Dav Reid Finale Handicap Stakes (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Raammee
runners_data.note: Won twice this season over 8f on good ground but has placed over 10f at Goodwood on good; Roger Varian yard in solid form (7/20 T14), Ray Dawson up, travels prominently and maps ideally in the first chase pack — 42 days off is fine for this stable.
runners_data.comment: Raammee arrives on the back of a win last time out, with three wins in his last five starts painting a picture of a horse in fine fettle, and his trainer's 30% strike rate over the past fortnight adds strong support; the main risk is the 42-day absence since that victory.

runners_data.name: Thunder Run
runners_data.note: Five-year-old who has shown ability at this trip (2nd/10f Good, 3rd/15 on similar going) but poor recent form including a 15th; Clifford Lee rides and prominent style suits the shape, though a string of misfires in 2025 demands caution.
runners_data.comment: Thunder Run arrives here rated 108 by our assessors and ranked second of 21 — a strong profile — with experience over today's trip and ground, though he carries 136 lb from stall 13 and has been winless in recent starts, including a second three starts back sandwiched by less encouraging efforts.

runners_data.name: Erzindjan
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse for Ryan Moore; won over 9f on good last time out and has soft-ground form (8th/10f Soft), but eight-year-old getting further at this trip with only 2/15 on similar going — Moore could weave through but profile is against the dominant shape.
runners_data.comment: Erzindjan won two starts back and has experience of today's trip and going, giving him a solid profile under 136 lb; the 66-day absence is worth noting, but his rating of 110 marks him as the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Diego El Queso
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type who has won over 10f on soft and placed five times on similar going; Gary Carroll rides for G M Lyons and this horse's best form genuinely comes from off the pace, making him one of the more credible deep closers if a gap appears.
runners_data.comment: Diego El Queso showed smart form with a win three starts back and a runner-up finish two starts back, but his sixth last time out tempers confidence; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 135 lb from stall 16, and our rating of 102 suggests he holds claims without dominating.

runners_data.name: Dain Ma Nut In
runners_data.note: Hold-up five-year-old with a 7lb claimer aboard; won over 10f on Good and has some soft-going exposure, but 0/15 on similar going and a field of 22 makes getting a clear late run very difficult from out the back.
runners_data.comment: Placed last time out and a winner four starts back, Dain Ma Nut In has experience of today's distance and going in his favour, though he must shoulder 133 lb from stall 17 and our rating of 94 leaves him with ground to find on the pick of these.

runners_data.name: Al Aali
runners_data.note: William Buick takes the mount for George Scott on a four-year-old who has won twice in succession over 10f on good; wears blinkers, hold-up style, and three soft-going starts returned 0W2P — the booking of Buick is the standout positive here.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins give Al Aali strong recent momentum, and he has run over today's trip before, but a rating of 97 and a tendency to struggle in the deeper stages of his recent sequence give pause, with 133 lb from stall nine adding to the ask.

runners_data.name: Quai De Bethune
runners_data.note: James Doyle partner for Hamad Al Jehani; ran well enough to win over 10f earlier in the season but last three are all 6th or worse; one soft-going run, prominent style suits the map position but recent form is flat.
runners_data.comment: Quai De Bethune has run over today's distance and going, and a win four starts back gives his record some substance, but two unplaced efforts in his last two starts are a concern at 129 lb from stall seven against a field of 21.

runners_data.name: King's Code
runners_data.note: Six-year-old wearing a visor for David Evans; only 1/15 on similar going and OR has slid from a peak, but ran 9 days ago so is racecourse fit and prominent style keeps him in the right part of the field tactically.

runners_data.name: Bourbon Blues
runners_data.note: Three-year-old for Brian Meehan with Oisin Murphy, a quality booking; placed at 10f on good and prominent style maps well — soft-ground record is limited but Murphy's ability to find a position off the pace is a significant asset in a congested field.
runners_data.comment: Bourbon Blues shaped with plenty of promise when second last time out, and he has experience over today's trip and going, with our rating of 107 putting him right in the mix; the concern is that he has been winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Have Secret
runners_data.note: Six-year-old wearing a visor for the Fahey yard; won over 10f on good and has 6/15 on similar going including soft, but last five include a run of zeros and the hold-up style from a crowded 22-runner field is problematic.
runners_data.comment: Have Secret won in his last five starts but has been unplaced in his two most recent outings, so he arrives needing to rediscover some form after 42 days off; experience over today's trip and going is a plus, though 128 lb from stall 12 adds to his task.

runners_data.name: Parole d'Oro
runners_data.note: Rossa Ryan rides for Michael Bell on a four-year-old wearing a tongue-tie; placed twice at 10f on good, prominent style fits the shape, but the trainer has 0 winners from 19 runners in the T14 window — cold yard flag.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Parole d'Oro does show a second three starts back to give connections hope, though a seventh last time out is the concern heading into this; he has run over today's trip and arrives fresh enough on 25 days' rest carrying 127 lb from stall 14.

runners_data.name: Accredit
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race; won twice on soft as a two-year-old for Gosden and returns after 309 days off — the key unknown is whether that layoff blunts sharpness, but if Colin Keane gets him rolling, he has an uncontested lead in a field that cannot easily reel him in.
runners_data.comment: A long absence of 309 days is the obvious concern for Accredit, and our figures rank him last of the 21 runners; however, his recent form does include back-to-back wins, and he has experience of today's going.

runners_data.name: Mr Swivell
runners_data.note: Five-year-old who was second over 8f on good and placed 0W2P in 4/15 on similar going; prominent style suits the congested shape tactically, though a step up to 10f in a big-field soft-ground handicap is a notable ask.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Mr Swivell at least posted a second two runs back and has experience of today's trip and going, though that eighth last time out is harder to ignore; 127 lb from stall 10 makes life no easier for a gelding ranked eighth of twenty-one.

runners_data.name: Castle Stuart
runners_data.note: Hold-up four-year-old who was third 14 days ago over 10f and won over 12f on good earlier; 1W2P from 6/15 on similar going is solid, Barry McHugh rides, and the drop to OR90 may have him well-handicapped — headgear (hood) confirmed.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Castle Stuart does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and a third and a second in recent outings show ability — but that ninth last time out is a concern, and a rating of 95 ranked twelfth of twenty-one suggests he faces a stiff task here.

runners_data.name: Dhahabi
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with a long losing run (0/00-00) and only 0W1P from 2/15 on similar going; genuine hold-up style from the rear in a 22-runner field on soft makes a win very unlikely at this stage of his career.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and drawn in stall 21, Dhahabi faces an uphill task with the trainer firing at just five per cent recently, though he has experience of today's trip and conditions and returns on a manageable 25-day break carrying 125 lb.

runners_data.name: Sujet
runners_data.note: Has won and placed over 8f on good ground and wears blinkers for Declan Carroll; a natural hold-up horse shuffled into a midfield mapping position because the field has too many closers for all to operate from the rear — his chance is compressed by racing out of role.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with unplaced efforts dominating a record that only two runner-up finishes relieve, Sujet is hard to fancy from stall 18 on these figures, though he has run over today's going before and returns after a 42-day break with conditions not entirely against him.

runners_data.name: Shafdar
runners_data.note: Wears a tongue-tie for Ian Williams (2/38 T14); won over 8f on good earlier in the season and ran only 21 days ago — a genuine hold-up type that cannot get to his favoured rearmost berth in this field, leaving him in a position that does not showcase his strengths.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well down the field on our figures and representing a trainer in poor current form, Shafdar is hard to fancy on bare merit, though he does return just three weeks after his last run and recorded a win four starts back to show he retains ability.

runners_data.name: Dark Moon Rising
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 10f on good wearing a hood for Kevin Ryan; his best form tends to come from prominent forward-tracking, but in this field there is no room at the front, meaning he operates from a deeper position than ideal — recent winning form is the positive.
runners_data.comment: Dark Moon Rising won last time out but has been largely out of the frame in recent starts otherwise, and with his trainer firing at just 4% over the past fortnight and he ranking 17th of 21 on our figures, there is little here to inspire confidence despite his experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Salam Dubawi
runners_data.note: Four-year-old for Jim Goldie (6/47 T14) with an apprentice claiming 5lbs; hold-up style with a Disqualification on the card, and with 0/11 on similar going the case is thin — one of the runners most compromised by the redistribution from their natural position.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 20 of 21 on our figures, Salam Dubawi is hard to fancy after finishing unplaced last time out, with a fourth two starts back and a disqualification three starts back blotting his recent record; he has run over today's trip and returns on a reasonable 28-day break, but his profile offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Nepal
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason rides for Ivan Furtado (0/14 T14); won over 12f on good and has placed twice at 10f, but a genuine hold-up type squeezed out of the rear by the depth of closers in this field — trainer has had no winners in 14 days and the amateur booking adds risk.
runners_data.comment: Ranked near the foot of the field on our figures, Nepal faces a stiff ask here — a winner three starts back, he was unplaced next time and fourth last time out, and a speed rating of 82 does little to inspire confidence, even if he has distance and going experience and lines up fresh enough from stall one.

runners_data.name: Rainbow Nebula
runners_data.note: Fahey-trained four-year-old wearing a hood; won over 8f on good and has 1W2P from 4/14 on similar going — prominent style is well-suited to the race map and Cam Hardie knows this stable, though OR85 means a big weight swing is needed.
runners_data.comment: Rainbow Nebula won five starts back but has been unplaced, fifth, or sixth in his four subsequent outings, suggesting he is out of form; experience over today's trip and going gives him a foothold, though 42 days off and a rating of 85 make improvement hard to envisage.

runners_data.name: Double Parked
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie, prominent style for Tim Easterby (4/84 T14); placed at 8f and 10f on good recently, racecourse fit after 11 days, and OR84 gives weight relief — Saffie Osborne claims 3lbs which helps, and prominent style puts him in the right place tactically.
runners_data.comment: Fifth last time out tempers any enthusiasm for Double Parked, and his trainer's woeful recent strike-rate of 5% gives little confidence; he has run over today's trip and going, but ranked 16 of 21 on our figures, he is hard to fancy from stall 15.

races.paceDynamic: Accredit is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 22-runner field and, with 309 days off the track, Colin Keane will look to exploit that lone-leader role by dictating a measured, sustainable gallop on Good to Soft ground over 1m2½f — a distance and surface the horse already handles well (3/3 sim-going). Behind Accredit, a congested group of nine prominent-style runners — including Raammee, Thunder Run, Quai De Bethune, King's Code, Bourbon Blues, Parole d'Oro, Mr Swivell, Rainbow Nebula and Double Parked — will contest the space from second to mid-pack, creating significant interference and potential traffic trouble from the 2-3f mark. The field holds more hold-up types than can realistically settle at the back: Sujet, Shafdar, Dark Moon Rising, Salam Dubawi and Nepal are genuine hold-up horses mapped to midfield because there is no room for all of them to fulfil their natural role, meaning true closers will be compromised. The tactical verdict is clear: with one uncontested lead, a sustainable pace, and prominent congestion choking off hold-up runners, horses who travel prominently in the first chase pack — within three to five lengths of Accredit — hold the decisive positional advantage, with genuine hold-up horses facing an uphill task from out-of-role positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Accredit Controls, Chasers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Accredit bowls along at a measured tempo and the prominent pack tracks efficiently without incident, leaving the closers in traffic.
scenarios.body: Accredit sets a controlled lead and the best-placed chasers in the prominent group cruise into contention turning in, with the soft ground premium going to those who travel smoothly just off the pace; the congestion in the prominent group matters less here because the pace is honest enough to string them out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Chaos, Front Holds
scenarios.trigger: If the nine prominent runners crowd each other badly at halfway, causing interference, and Accredit is left alone to coast clear.
scenarios.body: Accredit steals a widening advantage as the chasing pack burns energy jostling for positions 2-5, and the soft ground punishes horses who have wasted petrol early; only those prominent runners who have found clean air early can mount a late challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Sweep From Deep
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to compromise Accredit and the front group, and a clear late passage opens for closers.
scenarios.body: Those mapped-back hold-up types who happen to find room — most plausibly Diego El Queso or Al Aali, both genuine hold-up horses with course-distance profiles — could pick up the pieces if the prominent runners burn each other out; however, Sujet, Shafdar, Dark Moon Rising and Nepal are out of role and their chances in this scenario are materially discounted.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Slog, Stayer Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the going deteriorates significantly through the afternoon and the race becomes a thorough stamina test at the longest pace.
scenarios.body: A grinding, attrition-based finish would favour horses who have already proven themselves on soft ground at this trip or longer, eliminating lighter-framed or quick-ground specialists entirely; the prominent pack may find the soft surface nullifying early positional advantage and rewarding horses with proven stamina credentials.

watchPoints.text: Prominent congestion is severe — nine runners (Raammee, Thunder Run, Quai De Bethune, King's Code, Bourbon Blues, Parole d'Oro, Mr Swivell, Rainbow Nebula, Double Parked) are all hunting the same early positions 2-6, and interference or a pace injection from any one of them between the 3f and 2f markers could unsettle several fancied runners simultaneously.

Accredit returns after 309 days off the track for Gosden/Keane; if the layoff means he is not fully wound up and he cannot sustain the gallop into the straight, the entire pace dynamic collapses and the scenario probabilities shift sharply toward hold-up horses — monitor his warmup closely.

Sujet, Shafdar, Dark Moon Rising, Salam Dubawi and Nepal are all genuine hold-up types forced into a midfield slot by field congestion; any of them racing keen or wide trying to recover their natural position will waste energy and effectively remove themselves from contention.

The going is Good to Soft throughout the card at York today — if late-afternoon cut is marginally worse than earlier races, stamina becomes more of a premium and horses proven over further (Castle Stuart, Nepal, Dhahabi) could outrun their handicap marks at the expense of shorter-trip specialists.
